result.markdown: --- title: "🚧Unsupervised BNNC" description: "Bayesian Neural Network Clustering for discovering hidden multivariate groupings." categories: [Neural Networks, Classification, Unsupervised Learning] image: "Figures/24.png" order: 36 reading-time: true --- ## General Principles Building upon the [Dirichlet Process Mixture Model (DPMM)](25.%20DPMM.qmd) and the [Multiclass classification BNN](35.%20BNN%20for%20multiclass%20classification.qmd), the **Bayesian Neural Network Clustering (BNNC)** model can learn to separate unlabelled datasets into $K$ underlying mixture components using a deep gating network without observing any initial ground-truth classes. Rather than sampling discrete cluster assignments via categorical weights directly as a standard GMM, BNNC routes data points through a neural layer to output continuous mixing probabilities $\theta_i$. ## Considerations ::: callout-note - **Marginalized Likelihood**: The likelihood of any given observation is constructed by summing the probability density over all $K$ potential multivariate Gaussian clusters recursively weighted by the network's generated $\theta_i$ mixing assignments ([LogSumExp 🛈]{#logsumexp} trick). - **Parsimony Prior**: We enforce an explicit Dirichlet prior $Dir(\alpha / K)$ over the gating network weights. Supplying a concentration parameter $\alpha < 1$ acts as a severe sparsity constraint, ensuring the network drives unused clusters towards probability 0, mirroring the stick-breaking properties of DPMMs automatically. - **Consensus Clustering**: To determine actual hard cluster sizes after MCMC sampling, we construct an average adjacency matrix measuring how often points are paired together, and run hierarchical clustering on the complement distance matrix. ::: ## Example Below is an example code snippet demonstrating *Unsupervised BNNC* using the BayesForge (**BF**) package to locate hidden clusters from a $K=4$ synthetic target. ### Simulated Data ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Python (Raw) ```python from BayesForge import bf import jax.numpy as jnp import jax import numpyro import jax.scipy.stats as stats from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs # Setup device------------------------------------------------ m = bf(platform='cpu') # Generate Synthetic Data ------------------------------------ # 4 distinct underlying true clusters data, true_labels = make_blobs( n_samples=500, centers=4, cluster_std=0.8, center_box=(-10,10), random_state=101 ) m.data_on_model = dict(data=data) # Define raw model ------------------------------------------------ def bnn_mixture_model(data, K=11, D_H1=10): # data shape: (N, D) N, D_X = data.shape # --- BNN Gating Network --- w1 = m.bnn.layer_linear( data, dist=m.dist.normal(0, 1, name='w1_weight', shape=(D_X, D_H1)), activation='tanh' ) w2 = m.bnn.layer_linear( w1, dist=m.dist.normal(0, 0.05, name='w2_weight', shape=(D_H1, K)) ) # Global parsimony prior: Dirichlet prior on global cluster weights # Alpha < 1 acts as a sparse prior to suppress inactive clusters alpha = 0.05 pi = numpyro.sample('global_pi', numpyro.distributions.Dirichlet(jnp.ones(K) * (alpha / K))) logits = w2 + jnp.log(pi + 1e-10) log_p = jax.nn.log_softmax(logits, axis=-1) theta = jnp.exp(log_p) numpyro.deterministic('theta', theta) # --- Mixture Components --- mu = m.dist.normal(0, 5, name='mu', shape=(K, D_X)) sigma = m.dist.exponential(1.0, name='sigma', shape=(K, D_X)) # --- Marginalized Gaussian Mixture --- data_exp = jnp.expand_dims(data, axis=1) # (N, 1, D_X) mu_exp = jnp.expand_dims(mu, axis=0) # (1, K, D_X) sigma_exp = jnp.expand_dims(sigma, axis=0) # (1, K, D_X) log_pdf_clusters = jnp.sum(stats.norm.logpdf(data_exp, loc=mu_exp, scale=sigma_exp), axis=-1) # (N, K) weighted_log_pdf = log_p + log_pdf_clusters # (N, K) # LogSumExp merges K clusters back together total_log_likelihood = jax.scipy.special.logsumexp(weighted_log_pdf, axis=-1) # Target Likelihood numpyro.factor('mixture_likelihood', jnp.sum(total_log_likelihood)) # Run MCMC m.fit(bnn_mixture_model, num_chains=1) ``` ## Python (Build in function) ::: {#fd013f99 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from BayesForge import bf from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs m = bf() # Generate Synthetic Data ------------------------------------ data, true_labels = make_blobs( n_samples=500, centers=4, cluster_std=0.8, center_box=(-10,10), random_state=101 ) # K is the maximum component limit, D_H1 is the hidden width m.data_on_model = dict(data=data, K=11, D_H1=10, empirical_bayes=True) # Enables empirical priors over fixed standards # Run MCMC m.fit(m.models.bnnc, num_chains=1) # Predict cluster targets theta_samps, mu_samps, sigma_samps, labels = m.models.bnnc.predict(data, m.sampler) # Plot Results m.models.bnnc.plot(data, m.sampler) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` bf v 0.0.60 package loaded ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` An NVIDIA GPU may be present on this machine, but a CUDA-enabled jaxlib is not installed. BNNC unsupervised_files/figure-html/cell-2-output-7.png){} ::: ::: ## R (Raw) ```r library(BayesForge) m <- importBF(platform = "cpu") jax <- reticulate::import("jax") jnp <- reticulate::import("jax.numpy") numpyro <- reticulate::import("numpyro") stats <- reticulate::import("jax.scipy.stats") # Generate Synthetic Data ------------------------------------ # 4 distinct underlying true clusters sk <- reticulate::import("sklearn.datasets") out <- sk$make_blobs( n_samples = 500L, centers = 4L, cluster_std = 0.8, center_box = reticulate::tuple(-10, 10), random_state = 101L ) data <- out[[1]] true_labels <- out[[2]] m$data_on_model <- list(data = data) # Define raw model ------------------------------------------------ # BF passes only `data` (an R matrix here); K and D_H1 keep their defaults bnn_mixture_model <- function(data, K = 11L, D_H1 = 10L) { # data shape: (N, D) N <- dim(data)[1] D_X <- dim(data)[2] # --- BNN Gating Network --- w1 <- m$bnn$layer_linear( data, dist = m$dist$normal(0, 1, name = "w1_weight", shape = reticulate::tuple(D_X, D_H1)), activation = "tanh" ) w2 <- m$bnn$layer_linear( w1, dist = m$dist$normal(0, 0.05, name = "w2_weight", shape = reticulate::tuple(D_H1, K)) ) # Global parsimony prior: Dirichlet prior on global cluster weights # Alpha < 1 acts as a sparse prior to suppress inactive clusters alpha <- 0.05 pi <- numpyro$sample("global_pi", numpyro$distributions$Dirichlet(jnp$ones(K) * (alpha / K))) logits <- w2 + jnp$log(pi + 1e-10) log_p <- jax$nn$log_softmax(logits, axis = -1L) theta <- jnp$exp(log_p) numpyro$deterministic("theta", theta) # --- Mixture Components --- mu <- m$dist$normal(0, 5, name = "mu", shape = reticulate::tuple(K, D_X)) sigma <- m$dist$exponential(1.0, name = "sigma", shape = reticulate::tuple(K, D_X)) # --- Marginalized Gaussian Mixture --- data_exp <- jnp$expand_dims(data, axis = 1L) # (N, 1, D_X) mu_exp <- jnp$expand_dims(mu, axis = 0L) # (1, K, D_X) sigma_exp <- jnp$expand_dims(sigma, axis = 0L) # (1, K, D_X) log_pdf_clusters <- jnp$sum(stats$norm$logpdf(data_exp, loc = mu_exp, scale = sigma_exp), axis = -1L) # (N, K) weighted_log_pdf <- log_p + log_pdf_clusters # (N, K) # LogSumExp merges K clusters back together total_log_likelihood <- jax$scipy$special$logsumexp(weighted_log_pdf, axis = -1L) # Target Likelihood numpyro$factor("mixture_likelihood", jnp$sum(total_log_likelihood)) } # Run MCMC m$fit(bnn_mixture_model, num_chains = 1L) ``` ## R (Build in function) ```r library(BayesForge) m <- importBF() # Generate Synthetic Data ------------------------------------ sk <- reticulate::import("sklearn.datasets") out <- sk$make_blobs( n_samples = 500L, centers = 4L, cluster_std = 0.8, center_box = reticulate::tuple(-10, 10), random_state = 101L ) data <- out[[1]] true_labels <- out[[2]] # K is the maximum component limit, D_H1 is the hidden width m$data_on_model <- list(data = data, K = 11L, D_H1 = 10L, empirical_bayes = TRUE) # Enables empirical priors over fixed standards # Run MCMC m$fit(m$models$bnnc, num_chains = 1L) # Predict cluster targets pred <- m$models$bnnc$predict(data, m$sampler) theta_samps <- pred[[1]] mu_samps <- pred[[2]] sigma_samps <- pred[[3]] labels <- pred[[4]] # Plot Results m$models$bnnc$plot(data, m$sampler) ``` ## Julia (Raw) ```julia using PyBayesForge using PythonCall # Setup device------------------------------------------------ m = importBF(platform="cpu") numpyro = pyimport("numpyro") stats = pyimport("jax.scipy.stats") # Generate Synthetic Data ------------------------------------ # 4 distinct underlying true clusters sk = pyimport("sklearn.datasets") out = sk.make_blobs( n_samples=500, centers=4, cluster_std=0.8, center_box=(-10, 10), random_state=101 ) data = out[0] true_labels = out[1] m.data_on_model = pydict(data = data) # Define raw model ------------------------------------------------ # BF calls the model with `data` only, so K and D_H1 are set inside the body @BF function bnn_mixture_model(data) K = 11 D_H1 = 10 # data shape: (N, D) N = data.shape[0] D_X = data.shape[1] # --- BNN Gating Network --- w1 = m.bnn.layer_linear( data, dist=m.dist.normal(0, 1, name="w1_weight", shape=(D_X, D_H1)), activation="tanh" ) w2 = m.bnn.layer_linear( w1, dist=m.dist.normal(0, 0.05, name="w2_weight", shape=(D_H1, K)) ) # Global parsimony prior: Dirichlet prior on global cluster weights # Alpha < 1 acts as a sparse prior to suppress inactive clusters alpha = 0.05 pi = numpyro.sample("global_pi", numpyro.distributions.Dirichlet(jnp.ones(K) * (alpha / K))) logits = w2 + jnp.log(pi + 1e-10) log_p = jax.nn.log_softmax(logits, axis=-1) theta = jnp.exp(log_p) numpyro.deterministic("theta", theta) # --- Mixture Components --- mu = m.dist.normal(0, 5, name="mu", shape=(K, D_X)) sigma = m.dist.exponential(1.0, name="sigma", shape=(K, D_X)) # --- Marginalized Gaussian Mixture --- data_exp = jnp.expand_dims(data, axis=1) # (N, 1, D_X) mu_exp = jnp.expand_dims(mu, axis=0) # (1, K, D_X) sigma_exp = jnp.expand_dims(sigma, axis=0) # (1, K, D_X) log_pdf_clusters = jnp.sum(stats.norm.logpdf(data_exp, loc=mu_exp, scale=sigma_exp), axis=-1) # (N, K) weighted_log_pdf = log_p + log_pdf_clusters # (N, K) # LogSumExp merges K clusters back together total_log_likelihood = jax.scipy.special.logsumexp(weighted_log_pdf, axis=-1) # Target Likelihood numpyro.factor("mixture_likelihood", jnp.sum(total_log_likelihood)) end # Run MCMC m.fit(bnn_mixture_model, num_chains=1) ``` ## Julia (Build in function) ```julia using PyBayesForge using PythonCall m = importBF() # Generate Synthetic Data ------------------------------------ sk = pyimport("sklearn.datasets") out = sk.make_blobs( n_samples=500, centers=4, cluster_std=0.8, center_box=(-10, 10), random_state=101 ) data = out[0] true_labels = out[1] # K is the maximum component limit, D_H1 is the hidden width m.data_on_model = pydict(data = data, K = 11, D_H1 = 10, empirical_bayes = true) # Enables empirical priors over fixed standards # Run MCMC m.fit(m.models.bnnc, num_chains=1) # Predict cluster targets pred = m.models.bnnc.predict(data, m.sampler) theta_samps, mu_samps, sigma_samps, labels = pred[0], pred[1], pred[2], pred[3] # Plot Results @pyplot m.models.bnnc.plot(data, m.sampler) ``` ::: ## Mathematical Details In the Bayesian formulation, we place [priors 🛈]{#prior} on all weights and biases and define a likelihood for the output. For a BNNC model with a $K$-hidden-layer gating network and a $D_X$-vector of predictors we can run the model as below. For the code example, we consider a single hidden layer gating network with a hyperbolic tangent ($\tanh$) [activation function 🛈]{#Activation}. Because the input matrix $X$ incorporates the intercept as its first column, the bias term is implicitly included in the layer's weights: $$ \begin{aligned} \log p(X_i \mid \mu, \sigma, \theta) & = \text{LogSumExp} \left[ \log(\theta_{ik}) + \log \mathcal{N}(X_i \mid \mu_k, \sigma_k) \right]_{k=1}^K \\ \theta_i & = \text{Softmax}(\phi_i) \\ \phi_i & = H_i W_2 + \log(\pi) \\ H_i & = \tanh(X_i W_1) \\ \pi & \sim \text{Dirichlet}(\frac{\alpha}{K}, \dots, \frac{\alpha}{K}) \\ W_1 & \sim \text{Normal}(0, 1) \\ W_2 & \sim \text{Normal}(0, 0.05) \\ \mu_k & \sim \text{Normal}(0, 5) \\ \sigma_k & \sim \text{Exponential}(1) \\ \end{aligned} $$ where: * $X_i$ is the observed data vector for the $i$-th observation. * $\theta_{ik}$ is the probability of assigning observation $i$ to component $k$. * $\pi$ is the global cluster weight vector, which enforces parsimony via a Dirichlet prior. * $\alpha$ is the concentration parameter (e.g., 0.05), driving unused clusters towards zero. * $H_i$ is the hidden layer representation vector for the $i$-th observation ($D_H = 10$). * $W_1$ and $W_2$ are the weight matrices of the gating network. * $\mu_k$ and $\sigma_k$ are the mean and standard deviation for the $k$-th Gaussian mixture component. * All gating network weights are assigned independent Normal priors. ## Model validation tests - [Documentation examples](https://github.com/BGN-for-ASNA/BF/tree/main/Test/3.Documentation): the Python examples of this page are run by the documentation tests (`Python/test_model_pages.py`). ## Reference(s) 1. Murphy, K. P. (2012). *Machine Learning: A Probabilistic Perspective*. MIT Press.
